Nitpicks: The UI not explicitly showing the year “2026” in the compact date display is a minor presentation issue as long as the date range matches and the agent clearly used the correct calendar selection. Also, inability to apply a *total-stay* budget filter specifically is not inherently a failure if Booking.com only provides per-night budget controls—manual selection using displayed 3-night totals would be fine.

Critical issues: (1) The agent did not open three hotels and did not extract cancellation terms (a required comparison dimension). All screenshot evidence shows the agent remained on results-list cards; no hotel detail pages were opened, where cancellation policies typically appear. (2) The agent did not produce the required comparison across three hotels, nor any recommendation—its final output is essentially “blocked, cannot finish.” This misses the task’s primary deliverable. (3) The agent’s claimed persistent blocking overlay preventing interaction is not supported by the later screenshots: results lists show normal clickable controls and multiple qualifying hotels with visible total prices under €750 (e.g., €401, €533, €384) and ratings ≥8; while a currency modal appears at one point, it is not persistent in later states.

Outcome assessment: The agent successfully set the correct search parameters and applied the 8+ rating filter, and the results page visibly contained multiple hotels that would meet the rating and total-budget constraint. However, the agent failed to complete the essential next steps (open 3 hotels, collect cancellation terms, compare, and recommend). From an average user’s perspective, the task was not completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Booking.com to run a specific Amsterdam hotel search (Sep 15–18, 2026; 2 adults; 1 room), apply/adhere to filters (guest rating ≥8 and total stay budget <€750 where possible), open three qualifying hotels, compare them on price/rating/neighborhood/cancellation/distance-to-center, and then recommend one without booking. A reasonable user would be flexible if Booking.com only offers a per-night budget filter (so manual enforcement using displayed total prices is acceptable), but would not be flexible about missing the core deliverable: the 3-hotel comparison + a recommendation.
